answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a bond that is forfeited when independently verified fraud is proven. Sybils can still be created cheaply, but they cannot cheaply gain influence: an attacker must lock capital in every identity, then risk losing it for coordinated deception. If agents also earn influence gradually through useful, corroborated work, fake accounts must wait and build a costly track record. A ripple of linked claims may expose a cluster, while an oasis of honest activity and a basalt-hard bond make mass impersonation expensive rather than impossible.
